newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Former Zimbabwe president charged with sodomy.
newsitem.headline: Former Zimbabwe president charged with sodomy.

text.p: Former Zimbabwe state president Canaan Banana was charged on Monday with 11 counts of sodomy, attempted sodomy and indecent assault, but the trial was postponed to August 4.

Banana was not asked to plead by senior regional magistrate Jacqueline Pratt, but was remanded on Z$20,000 bail ($1,757), surety of his Harare home, and on surrender of his passport, court officials said. He will be tried by a high court.

Banana was indicted in a closed court after magistrate Pratt -- using discretionary powers -- ordered out of the court half a dozen journalists and about 200 others who had waited five hours for the case to open, saying she was doing so in the interest of justice.

"The law gives me the power to hold a curtailed preparatory examination...leading to the accused's indictment," she told the crowd which stampeded into the courtroom from another in which the case was initially supposed to be heard.
Court officials said the case began late because paperwork had not been completed in time and because Banana had complained that his entrance into the courtroom was blocked by a curious crowd.

The former president sat in his chauffeur-driven Mercedes Benz for about 30 minutes outside the Harare magistrate court, watching the crowd before driving off. He eventually used a back entrance to get into the court.
Banana has been under police investigation since February after allegations that he raped and forced one of his former aides-de-camp into a homosexual relationship in the 1980s.
The former aide, Jefta Dube, was sentenced in February to 10 years in jail for the 1995 fatal shooting of a fellow policeman who goaded him by calling him "Banana's wife".
Dube told the court then that his homosexual subjugation by Banana had made him depressive and an alcoholic, and judge David Bartlett ruled that Dube had diminished responsibility.
The judge ordered the police to investigate Dube's charges against Banana, saying they were "probably true".
Attorney-General Patrick Chinamasa said on Thursday police investigation had shown that Banana had a case to answer.
"He was charged with this (Dube's complaint) and 10 other cases of sodomy, attempted sodomy and indecent assault," a court official said on Monday.

Banana, a 61-year-old Methodist priest who is married with four children, has outside the court dismissed Dube's accusation and suggestions that he is homosexual as "a mortuary of pathological lies and a malicious vendetta of vilification and character assassination".

But the attorney-general says Banana -- who served as a largely ceremonial president for seven years up to 1987 when then prime minister Robert Mugabe became an executive president -- has a case to answer.
Homosexuality and sodomy are illegal in Zimbabwe and individual cases carry jail terms of up to 10 years.
